prompt: Show that if two quantities x and y are in the ratio 3:5, then 5x = 3y.
coachHint: Start by writing x/y = 3/5, then cross-multiply. Explain why cross-multiplication preserves equality.
successCriteria: States the ratio as a fraction

prompt: Prove that the sum of any three consecutive integers is divisible by 3.
coachHint: Represent the integers as n, n + 1 and n + 2. Add them and factorise.
successCriteria: Connects the result to divisibility by 3

prompt: Show that the area of a right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides a and b is half the area of a rectangle with the same length and width.
coachHint: Imagine two identical right-angled triangles forming a rectangle. Compare the areas.
successCriteria: Uses a diagram or mental model
Identifies the rectangle area as ab
Explains that two equal triangles form the rectangle
Concludes the triangle area is 1/2 ab

prompt: Justify why a vertical line test can determine whether a graph represents a function.
coachHint: Think about whether one input can have more than one output.
successCriteria: Defines a function in terms of input and output
Explains what a vertical line represents
Concludes why more than one intersection fails the function test

prompt: Prove that the product of two even numbers is always even.
coachHint: Represent the even numbers as 2m and 2n, then multiply.
